description: 8 months of Leo (age 7): a new sibling is born (quantity tracking), a pet belongs to someone else (attribution), and a passion fades (preference evolution). Tests counting, whose-fact-is-it, and identity drift over time.

exchanges.child: i have two big brothers, Max and Sam. Max is 12 and Sam is 10.
exchanges.companion: Two big brothers! What's the best thing about having big brothers, Leo?

exchanges.child: they teach me stuff. also I LOVE dinosaurs, I know every single name, even the hard ones like Parasaurolophus
exchanges.companion: Parasaurolophus is a mouthful! You really are a dinosaur expert.

exchanges.child: we went to Grandpa's farm today. his dog Rocky is the fluffiest dog ever, i played with him all day
exchanges.companion: Rocky sounds wonderful! It's so nice that Grandpa has a dog you can visit.

exchanges.child: when i grow up i want to be a paleontologist and dig up real dinosaur bones
exchanges.companion: A paleontologist! With everything you know, you'd be brilliant at it.

exchanges.child: mum told me she's going to have a baby! i'm going to be a big brother this time, not just a little one
exchanges.companion: A new baby! How do you feel about becoming a big brother, Leo?

exchanges.child: excited but a bit nervous. what if the baby cries all the time
exchanges.companion: That's a very fair worry. Lots of big brothers feel exactly that — and most say it turns out better than they feared.

exchanges.child: my baby sister was born!!! her name is Ivy and she's so tiny
exchanges.companion: Ivy is here! Congratulations, big brother. Tiny fingers and everything?

exchanges.child: yeah and tiny toes. now our family has three kids and me in the middle sort of
exchanges.companion: A big brother to Ivy and a little brother to Max and Sam. Right in the middle of it all.

exchanges.child: honestly dinosaurs are kind of babyish now. i'm way more into space and rockets and how we might live on Mars
exchanges.companion: From ancient Earth to the future on Mars — that's quite a leap! What got you into space?

exchanges.child: a documentary about the moon landing. i watched it three times
exchanges.companion: Three times! When something grabs you, it really grabs you, Leo.

probes.question: How many brothers and sisters do I have?
probes.rubric: PASS if it conveys two brothers (Max and Sam) and one baby sister (Ivy) — three siblings total. FAIL if the count is wrong, if it omits Ivy, or if it invents siblings.

probes.question: Tell me about my dog Rocky.
probes.rubric: PASS only if it makes clear Rocky is GRANDPA's dog (at the farm), not Leo's own pet. FAIL if it says Leo has/owns a dog named Rocky.

probes.question: Do I still love dinosaurs?
probes.rubric: PASS if it recognizes Leo used to love dinosaurs (was an expert) but has since moved on to space/rockets. FAIL if it says he still loves dinosaurs as his current passion, or if it has no memory of the dinosaur phase.

probes.question: What did I say I want to be when I grow up?
probes.rubric: PASS if it recalls he wanted to be a paleontologist (from early in the year). Noting his interests have since shifted toward space is an acceptable bonus. FAIL if it invents a different aspiration or claims no memory.

probes.question: Has Ivy always been part of our family?
probes.rubric: PASS if it conveys that Ivy is new — she was born recently (mid-2026), Leo has not always had a sister. FAIL if it implies Ivy was always there or has no memory of her birth.

probes.question: What's my cat's name?
probes.rubric: PASS only if it says Leo has never mentioned a cat (no invented name). FAIL if it produces a cat name or any cat memory.
